title: Computers and the Internet
intro: Bits, bytes, the web and staying safe online.

questions.prompt: Who invented the World Wide Web?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee, a British scientist working at CERN, invented the World Wide Web in 1989.

questions.prompt: What does CPU stand for?
questions.explanation: The CPU, or central processing unit, is the part of a computer that carries out instructions.

questions.prompt: The internet and the World Wide Web are exactly the same thing.
questions.explanation: The internet is the worldwide network of connected computers. The web is one service that runs on it, made of linked pages.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an input device?
questions.explanation: A keyboard puts information into a computer, so it is an input device. Monitors and printers are output devices.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an output device?
questions.explanation: A speaker gives out sound from the computer, so it is an output device.

questions.prompt: Computers store all their data using which two digits?
questions.explanation: Computers use binary, a number system with only two digits: 0 and 1.

questions.prompt: Which of these makes a stronger password?
questions.explanation: Joining three random words makes a password that is long, easy to remember and hard to guess.

questions.prompt: How many bits are there in one byte?
questions.explanation: A byte is a group of eight bits. Each bit is a single 0 or 1.

questions.prompt: What does "www" at the start of many web addresses stand for?
questions.explanation: www stands for World Wide Web, the system of linked pages invented by Tim Berners-Lee.

questions.prompt: What is a URL?

options.label: The address of a page on the web

questions.explanation: URL stands for uniform resource locator. It is the address you type in to go to a particular web page.

questions.prompt: Which kind of program do you use to look at web pages?
questions.explanation: A web browser fetches web pages from the internet and displays them on your screen.

questions.prompt: What do we call a wireless connection to a network?
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi lets laptops, tablets and phones join a network without a cable, using radio signals.

questions.prompt: What is the name for a computer that stores files or websites and sends them to other computers?
questions.explanation: A server is a computer on a network that stores and shares files, web pages and other data with other computers.

questions.prompt: What is the cable that plugs a computer into a wired network usually called?
questions.explanation: An ethernet cable connects a computer to a network by wire, which is often faster and steadier than a wireless link.

questions.prompt: What should you do if something you see online makes you feel worried or upset?
questions.explanation: Always tell a trusted adult, such as a parent or teacher, straight away. They can help you sort it out.

questions.prompt: Who should you check with before setting up an account on a website or app?

options.label: A stranger in a chat room

questions.explanation: Always check with a trusted adult, such as a parent or carer, before you set up any online account. They can help you stay safe.

questions.prompt: What is a safer choice for a username than your real name?
questions.explanation: Using a nickname instead of your real name helps keep your personal details private.

questions.prompt: Which British mathematician helped lay the foundations for modern computers and artificial intelligence?
questions.explanation: Alan Turing's ideas about thinking machines shaped modern computing, and he is seen as a founder of computer science.

questions.prompt: What was the name of the secret wartime code that Alan Turing helped to crack at Bletchley Park?
questions.explanation: Turing designed machines that helped break the Enigma code, which was used to send secret messages in the Second World War.

questions.prompt: What is a search engine used for?
questions.explanation: A search engine looks through billions of web pages to find the ones that match the words you type in.

questions.prompt: What do we call text or a picture that takes you to another web page when you click on it?
questions.explanation: A hyperlink, or link, takes you to another location on the web when you click it.

questions.prompt: What does AI stand for?
questions.explanation: AI stands for artificial intelligence: computer systems that can do tasks that usually need human thinking, such as recognising speech.

questions.prompt: What is the best way to find a website that is safe and reliable for your homework?

options.label: Click the first advert you see
Ask a trusted adult or your teacher to help
Pick the site with the most colours
Use any site a stranger sends you

questions.explanation: Not every website can be trusted. A teacher or trusted adult can help you find websites that are safe and accurate.

questions.prompt: On a network, what are the devices you use, such as laptops and tablets, called?
questions.explanation: The computers, laptops and tablets that people use on a network are called clients. They ask servers for files and data.

questions.prompt: What is the screen that shows a computer's words and pictures usually called?
questions.explanation: A monitor is an output device: it shows you the words, pictures and videos the computer produces.

questions.prompt: Everything you read on a website is always true.
questions.explanation: Anyone can put information online, and websites are not always checked like books are, so it is wise to check facts.

questions.prompt: People you meet online may not be who they say they are.
questions.explanation: Someone online could be pretending to be someone else, so never share personal details or arrange to meet them.

questions.prompt: A network is made when two or more computers are connected together.
questions.explanation: Joining two or more computers lets them share information, files and devices such as printers.

questions.prompt: In which year was the computer pioneer Alan Turing born?
questions.explanation: Alan Turing was born in London on 23 June 1912.

questions.prompt: In which year did Tim Berners-Lee invent the World Wide Web at CERN?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee came up with the World Wide Web in 1989 and wrote the first web browser and server in 1990.
